key_insight: Structured environmental noise makes photon loss Fock-state dependent, deforming errors beyond the space a bosonic quantum code is designed to correct.
engineering_relevance: Bosonic quantum error correction should account for environmental spectra and state-dependent dissipation rather than assume ideal photon-loss errors.
method: Inject spectrally engineered noise into a weakly nonlinear oscillator in a three-dimensional circuit-QED system.
Compare measured Fock-state dynamics with second-order time-convolutionless theory.
Apply narrowband noise to a binomially encoded logical qubit to probe error-space deformation.
evidence_signal: Measured dynamics show frequency-selective, non-Markovian transients consistent with theory, while long-time transition rates approach the Markovian limit.
watch_item: The abstract does not quantify the resulting logical error penalty under naturally occurring environmental noise.
paper_title: Impact of structured noise on bosonic quantum error correction
